## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to introduce a dynamic control plane, maintain per-device data quality, and verify end‑to‑end observability in a beginner pipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Kinesis with required correlationId
- Control stream feeding DynamoDB quotas
- Lambda processing with per-record sampling and dedupe
- S3 Parquet storage with date partitioning
- DLQ routing for invalid records
- X-Ray trace propagation
- LocalStack end-to-end testing

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-code: Lambda processing per-record
const rate = await getRateFromDynamo(event.correlationId);
if (Math.random() > rate) return; // apply sampling
if (!validate(event)) pushToDLQ(event);
await writeToS3Parquet(event);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test sampling accuracy and DLQ coverage in LocalStack?
- How would you monitor throughput, latency, and DLQ growth over time?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason about dynamic, production-grade routing and cost controls in a multi-tenant telemetry pipeline using AWS DVA. It also probes understanding of exactly-once guarantees, schema evolution, and end-to-end observability.

## Key Concepts
- Adaptive routing: per-tenant path selection between Lambda and Fargate
- Exactly-once delivery and idempotent writes
- Per-tenant quotas and backpressure
- Schema evolution for optional fields with Glue/Athena
- Canary rollout and rollback with feature flags
- OpenTelemetry tracing across all components

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo routing decision (per-tenant)
function selectPath(tenantId, rate, sla) {
  const cfg = routingTable[tenantId];
  if (!cfg) return 'lambda';
  if (rate > cfg.threshold || sla < 99.9) return cfg.enrichPath; // 'fargate' or 'lambda'
  return 'lambda';
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you model backfill consistency if a tenant skips data for a day?
- What metrics and alarms ensure SLA adherence under burst traffic?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical knowledge of data masking, data residency, retention governance, and auditing in real-world AWS DVA pipelines. Requires integrating Kinesis/Data Streams, Lambda/Fargate, S3 with Object Lock, Glue cataloging, Athena queries, and a DLQ for auditability. Also evaluates replay strategies without exposing PII.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-scoped masking policies and a centralized policy store (DynamoDB)
- Ingress processing with Lambda/Fargate per-tenant logic
- Dual-path storage: redacted data in regional S3 Parquet, raw data in immutable bucket
- Data retention controls via Glue Catalog tables and Athena views
- Audit visibility via Dead Letter Queue
- Replay semantics using raw data with idempotent re-ingest

## Code Example

```javascript
function maskPII(record, policy) {
  // simplistic example: redact email and phone if policy requires
  if (policy.redact.includes('email')) record.email = 'REDACTED@domain.com';
  if (policy.redact.includes('phone')) record.phone = 'REDACTED';
  return record;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test masking correctness and retention compliance across tenants?
- What are the latency, storage, and cost trade-offs of maintaining raw + redacted copies and enabling replay?
